findings.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The `include_website_name` method is defined without the question mark that Discourse's serializer framework looks for when conditionally including attributes. Discourse's conditional-attribute protocol dispatches to `include_website_name?`; the undecorated method is never invoked, so `website_name` is serialized unconditionally as `null` for users with no website, bloating every user-card and profile payload with a null key instead of omitting it — a payload-size and API-contract smell for all clients.

[ADVISORY] `URI(website.to_s)` is re-parsed up to twice per call (once for host, again for path) inside a serializer that runs for every user in list endpoints. Doubled URI parsing on a hot serialization path; the next refactor that adds another path-based branch multiplies the duplication. A single parsed local (`uri = URI(website.to_s) rescue nil`) deletes one parse and the repeated rescue-reliant pattern.

[ADVISORY] The hostname comparison is case-sensitive on `Discourse.current_hostname` while `URI#host` is downcased, so a site whose `current_hostname` setting contains uppercase (e.g. 'Example.com') never matches a downcased website host even when the domains are identical. Users on an instance configured with a mixed-case hostname see 'example.com/user' rendered as just 'example.com' (the path display this PR exists to provide), and the tests pass only because they stub all-lowercase hostnames.

[ADVISORY] `website_name` drops the query string and fragment of the website URL because it appends only `URI(...).path`. A user whose website is `http://example.com/page?id=123` on a same-domain instance gets a displayed link text of `example.com/page` — misleading but not broken; anyone needing the full URL in the label is bitten.

[BUG] The www-subdomain case falls through to the wrong branch and silently drops the path: website 'http://www.example.com/user' on an instance hosted at example.com returns only 'www.example.com'. When hostname lengths are equal and <= 2 (both registrable domains), the second branch is skipped (requires > 2 parts) and the else branch tests discourse_host.ends_with?('.www.example.com'), which is false, so the user sees 'www.example.com' instead of 'www.example.com/user' — precisely the same-instance-domain case this PR claims to handle, just via the www alias. No spec covers this case.

[ADVISORY] Host comparison is case-sensitive, so a website entered as 'http://Example.com/user' on an example.com instance fails the equality check and drops the path. Users who typed a mixed-case URL (URI#host preserves case) lose the path display on their profile even though the domain matches; browsers treat the hosts as identical, so the user perceives inconsistent behavior.

[ADVISORY] When the website is the site root ('http://example.com/'), website_name becomes 'example.com/' with a trailing slash. Users with a bare-domain website get a profile link label ending in '/', cosmetic but visible site-wide on every profile and user card.

[ADVISORY] The new tests cover only the true side of the equal-length->2-part branch (forums.example.com vs example.com) and never the false side (e.g. website 'forum.other.com' vs instance 'forums.example.com' returns bare host) nor the www-vs-apex case, leaving the branchy hostname logic without negative-path verification. A future refactor of the split/join comparison in website_name (the most fragile lines in this diff) can regress to always appending the path or never appending it without any spec failing; whoever touches user_serializer.rb next gets bitten.

[BUG] The 'complete URL path' returned by website_name drops the query string and fragment, so the displayed name is not the complete path for same-domain URLs with query parameters. A user whose website is 'http://example.com/t?post=12' on an instance hosted at example.com sees 'example.com/t' as the link text while the href still contains the query — the displayed text misrepresents the target, defeating the stated intent of showing the complete path.

[BUG] When the website URL has no path (e.g. 'http://example.com'), URI(website).path returns '/' and website_name becomes 'example.com/', showing a trailing slash that the pre-change host-only display never had. Same-domain profiles with bare-domain websites render the ugly 'example.com/' label on every user profile page, a visible regression against the old websiteName output.

[ADVISORY] The sibling-subdomain branch (equal label count, >2 labels) has no spec coverage in the diff, while every other branch does. The most intricate comparison in the method (e.g. 'forums.example.com' vs 'www.example.com') ships untested; a regression in the split/join logic would silently flip profiles between full-path and host-only display with no failing spec.

[ADVISORY] The method parses URI(website.to_s) twice per branch and embeds the multi-way domain comparison inline in the serializer, instead of extracting a single hostname-relationship helper. The next person who needs 'is this website on our domain?' (e.g. user card, admin views) will copy this 12-line conditional; extraction to one parsed-URI-based helper would delete the duplicate parses and give one place to fix the comparison rules.

[BUG] The sibling-subdomain heuristic compares registrable domains by raw label count and suffix equality, so two unrelated sites that share a multi-label public suffix are treated as the same domain. With the instance at bar.co.uk, a user whose website is http://foo.co.uk/some/long/private/path gets website_name "foo.co.uk/some/long/private/path" — the full URL path is displayed as if it were a trusted same-domain link, because website_host.split('.')[1..-1] ("co.uk") equals discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1] ("co.uk"). The equality test this whole feature rests on is wrong for any second-level TLD (.co.uk, .com.au, .org.br), in both directions: same-domain cases under those suffixes also fall through to label-count mismatches and silently degrade to host-only display.

[ADVISORY] website_name is built from URI(...).path only, dropping the query string and fragment, and re-parses the same URI up to three times per serialization. A same-domain profile link like http://example.com/t?topic=foo renders the link correctly in href but displays only "example.com/t", so the user-visible label misrepresents where the link goes; the repeated URI(website.to_s) construction is wasted work on every user serialization but is not a correctness issue.

[ADVISORY] The added tests cover only the matching-domain cases and never exercise a sibling-length host that should NOT match, so the false-positive sibling case (different site, equal label count) has no spec pinning it. A future refactor or the current heuristic's false-positive class (foo.co.uk vs bar.co.uk) ships green because the only equal-length test case is a genuine sibling; anyone changing the domain-matching logic gets no signal about unrelated-domain leakage.

[BUG] The sibling-length branch only matches subdomains of the same parent when both hosts have >2 labels, so a website of www.example.com on an instance hosted at example.com falls through to the parent-suffix branch which fails and returns the bare host, dropping the path. A user on an instance at example.com who sets website http://www.example.com/t/my-page sees the link text 'www.example.com' instead of 'www.example.com/t/my-page', violating the PR's stated objective of showing the complete path when the website domain is the same as the instance domain — the exact www-vs-apex case the code's own comment ('www.example.com == forum.example.com') claims to handle.

[ADVISORY] website_name concatenates only URI(...).path, discarding query strings and fragments from the website URL. A user whose website is http://example.com?t=signup (a common same-domain deep link) sees link text 'example.com' with no path at all, making the 'complete URL path' feature silently incomplete for any URL carrying a query or fragment.

[ADVISORY] A website value without a scheme (e.g. 'example.com/user' stored verbatim) makes URI(...).host return nil, so website_name is nil while include_website_name is true. The profile template's {{#if model.website_name}} guard hides the website row entirely even though a website is set; the old client-side websiteName computed had the same hole, but the diff's stated intent ('show complete URL path') is silently unmet for scheme-less input and no test covers it.

[ADVISORY] The 'same domain' matching was silently broadened from the PR's stated objective to treat sibling subdomains (www.example.com vs forum.example.com) and parent domains (example.com vs forums.example.com) as 'same', a semantic decision embedded in serializer control flow rather than explicitly accepted as the intent. Operators of multi-tenant or shared parent domains (e.g. any *.discourse.group-style hosting) will show users' full local paths — including potentially private topic paths — to viewers on sibling instances, a privacy/behavior change beyond the accepted 'same domain' scope; the next maintainer cannot tell from the code which equivalence rules were deliberately chosen vs accidental.

[ADVISORY] website_name compares URI host against Discourse.current_hostname without case normalization, so a mixed-case website URL ('http://EXAMPLE.com/user') fails the equality check even when the domains match. Users who enter a URL with uppercase host letters get the bare host shown instead of the full path — the feature this PR ships silently does not fire for them; a later fix that normalizes one side only will also create an inconsistent match surface.

[ADVISORY] The parent-domain branch treats any website sharing the instance's registrable suffix (any *.example.com when the forum runs on forums.example.com) as same-site and exposes the full URL path in the profile display. On multi-tenant or university-style domains (many unrelated departments under one parent domain), a user under a sibling subdomain gets another tenant's path surfaced in public profile listings — information disclosure of internal path structure that the previous host-only display intentionally omitted; the registrable-suffix logic is hand-rolled string splitting with no PSL awareness, so 'co.uk' style suffixes are also misjudged.

[ADVISORY] The second branch of UserSerializer#website_name (equal label-count sibling subdomains, e.g. website_host 'www.example.com' vs discourse_host 'forum.example.com') has no test that triggers it. A regression in the sibling-subdomain comparison (app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:141-144) — e.g. the split/join logic returning the bare host or misjoining the path — passes the full suite because no spec exercises a same-label-count case; checked spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb in this diff, which only covers exact-host match, different-domain, and parent-domain cases, never the www-vs-forum branch the code explicitly implements and comments.

[ADVISORY] The include_website_name guard (returns false when website is absent) is never tested, nor is the nil-return path when URI parsing fails. If website_name were emitted as a null key for users without a website (or the rescue-nil swallowed a case where website_name should be present), no spec fails; the existing 'with filled out website' context only asserts the present-website serialization, and there is no matching 'without website' context asserting json[:website_name] is absent.

goldens.comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/serializers/user_serializer.rb`, a conditional include hook is added as `def include_website_name` (no `?`). Discourse serializers typically use `include_<attr>?` methods to conditionally emit attributes; if the framework is dispatching to `include_website_name?`, this hook will never run and `:website_name` (added to `untrusted_attributes`) will be serialized for all users, producing `website_name: null` when `website` is blank. The diff shows no `include_website_name?` implementation, only the undecorated version, making the conditional omission likely broken.

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, the diff shows `URI(website.to_s)` being invoked multiple times per call: once for `.host` (`website_host = URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil`) and again for `.path` in several branches (`website_host + URI(website.to_s).path`). This is a concrete, diff-grounded inefficiency on a serializer path (not a correctness defect), and can be improved by parsing once into a local `uri` and reusing `uri.host`/`uri.path` while avoiding repeated `rescue` patterns.

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, `website_host` is derived from `URI(website.to_s).host` and then compared to `discourse_host = Discourse.current_hostname` using case-sensitive operations (`==`, `split`, `ends_with?`) without any normalization (e.g. `downcase`). If `current_hostname` contains uppercase/mixed case, identical domains won’t match and the method will take the wrong branch (e.g., returning only `website_host` instead of `website_host + path`). The spec stubs only lowercase hostnames, so it wouldn’t catch this.

adjudication.rationale: In `user_serializer.rb`, `website_name` builds the display label as `website_host + URI(website.to_s).path` in several branches, which inherently excludes `?query` and `#fragment` components. The template uses `model.website_name` only as the link text while the actual `href` remains `model.website`, so behavior isn’t broken, but the label can be misleading for same-domain/parent-domain cases where a user might expect the full URL to be reflected.

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, the described behavior is accurate: for `website_host = "www.example.com"` and `discourse_host = "example.com"`, the code skips the `website_host == discourse_host` branch and the “same-length > 2 parts” branch, then falls into the final `else`, where `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` is false and it returns just `website_host` (dropping `URI(...).path`). However, the diff does not establish that `www.example.com` should be treated as equivalent to `example.com` (the PR/specs only cover exact-host match and the case where the website host is a parent of the instance host). So this is a concrete, diff-grounded unhandled edge case / missing test for the new logic, but not a clearly verifiable defect against stated requirements.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Host comparison is case-sensitive, so a website entered as 'http://Example.com/user' on an example.com instance fails the equality check and drops the path. adjudication.rationale: The serializer compares `website_host = URI(website.to_s).host` to `Discourse.current_hostname` (both plain Ruby strings). While the finding claims `URI#host` preserves the original case (e.g., `Example.com`), Ruby’s standard `URI` parser normalizes the host to lowercase, so `URI('http://Example.com/user').host` becomes `example.com` and the equality branch would still match on an `example.com` instance, keeping the path (`website_host + URI(...).path`). The diff itself shows no evidence that mixed-case hosts would survive parsing and trigger the fallback branches.

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, when the instance hostname matches (or is a subdomain/parent-domain match) it returns `website_host + URI(website.to_s).path`. For a root URL like `http://example.com/`, `URI(...).path` is `/`, producing `example.com/`. The template now displays `{{model.website_name}}` as the link label, so the trailing slash would be visible. This differs from the previous client-side `website.split("/")[2]` behavior, which would have shown `example.com` without `/`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new tests cover only the true side of the equal-length->2-part branch (forums.example.com vs example.com) and never the false side (e.g. website 'forum.other.com' vs instance 'forums.example.com' returns bare host) nor the www-vs-apex case, leaving the branchy hostname logic without negative-path verification. adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial branching logic in `UserSerializer#website_name` (the `elsif (website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length) && discourse_host.split('.').length > 2` block and its ternary) but the added specs only exercise the `website_host == discourse_host` branch and the final `ends_with?` branch (e.g. `forums.example.com` vs `example.com`). No spec covers the equal-length-and->2 branch at all (neither its true nor false outcomes), nor cases like `forum.other.com` vs `forums.example.com` that should return the bare host. So the review concern about missing negative-path verification for the branchy hostname logic is grounded, even though the finding mislabels which branch the existing `forums.example.com` test hits.

adjudication.rationale: In `user_serializer.rb`, `website_name` builds the display string as `website_host + URI(website.to_s).path`, which necessarily omits `URI(...).query` and `URI(...).fragment`. So for same-domain URLs like `http://example.com/t?post=12#x`, the link text would be `example.com/t` while `href` remains the full URL. However, the diff’s tests and wording say “complete website path” (and use `.path`), which can reasonably be interpreted as excluding query/fragment, so it’s an unhandled edge case/expectation issue rather than a clearly verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] website_name concatenates only URI(...).path, discarding query strings and fragments from the website URL. A user whose website is http://example.com?t=signup (a common same-domain deep link) sees link text 'example.com' with no path at all, making the 'complete URL path' feature silently incomplete for any URL carrying a query or fragment.

adjudication.rationale: In `user_serializer.rb`, `website_name` builds the display string using `website_host + URI(website.to_s).path` in multiple branches. `URI(...).path` excludes query strings (`?t=...`) and fragments (`#...`), so for URLs where the “deep link” is only in the query/fragment (or where `path` is empty), the returned `website_name` will omit that information. This doesn’t break the actual link (the template still uses `href={{model.website}}`), but it makes the new “include path when same/related domain” display logic incomplete for those cases.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] A website value without a scheme (e.g. 'example.com/user' stored verbatim) makes URI(...).host return nil, so website_name is nil while include_website_name is true. The profile template's {{#if model.website_name}} guard hides the website row entirely even though a website is set; the old client-side websiteName computed had the same hole, but the diff's stated intent ('show complete URL path') is silently unmet for scheme-less input and no test covers it.

adjudication.rationale: In `user_serializer.rb`, `website_name` derives the host via `URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` and returns `nil` if the URI has no scheme (Ruby parses `"example.com/user"` as a path, so `host` is nil). But `include_website_name` only checks `website.present?`, so the attribute can be included while being nil. The template was changed to guard display on `{{#if model.website_name}}`, so scheme-less stored websites would still not render even though `model.website` is present, and the new “show complete URL path” behavior isn’t achieved for that input. The added specs only cover schemed URLs (`http://...`) and don’t cover this edge case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The 'same domain' matching was silently broadened from the PR's stated objective to treat sibling subdomains (www.example.com vs forum.example.com) and parent domains (example.com vs forums.example.com) as 'same', a semantic decision embedded in serializer control flow rather than explicitly accepted as the intent. Operators of multi-tenant or shared parent domains (e.g. any *.discourse.group-style hosting) will show users' full local paths — including potentially private topic paths — to viewers on sibling instances, a privacy/behavior change beyond the accepted 'same domain' scope; the next maintainer cannot tell from the code which equivalence rules were deliberately chosen vs accidental.

adjudication.rationale: The diff moves `websiteName` from a client-side host-only display (`website.split("/")[2]`) to a server-side `website_name` that sometimes appends `URI(...).path` when the instance hostname is considered “same” by broader equivalence rules: exact match (`website_host == discourse_host`), sibling subdomains with same parent when both have >2 labels (the `split('.').length`/`[1..-1]` comparison), and when the instance is a subdomain of the website host (`discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)`). This is a semantic expansion beyond strict same-host matching and will display full paths in those cases, whereas the old behavior always displayed just the host. Whether that’s desired is unclear from the code/comments and only partially covered by specs (no explicit sibling-subdomain test), so it’s a concrete scope/behavior concern rather than a provable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] website_name compares URI host against Discourse.current_hostname without case normalization, so a mixed-case website URL ('http://EXAMPLE.com/user') fails the equality check even when the domains match. Users who enter a URL with uppercase host letters get the bare host shown instead of the full path — the feature this PR ships silently does not fire for them; a later fix that normalizes one side only will also create an inconsistent match surface.

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, `website_host` is obtained via `URI(website.to_s).host`. Ruby’s `URI` parser normalizes the host to lowercase (e.g., parsing `http://EXAMPLE.com/user` yields `host == "example.com"`), so the mixed-case input described would not cause `website_host == discourse_host` to fail as claimed. The diff itself contains no evidence that `URI(...).host` preserves case, so the reported behavior is not verifiable from (and is inconsistent with) this implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The parent-domain branch treats any website sharing the instance's registrable suffix (any *.example.com when the forum runs on forums.example.com) as same-site and exposes the full URL path in the profile display. On multi-tenant or university-style domains (many unrelated departments under one parent domain), a user under a sibling subdomain gets another tenant's path surfaced in public profile listings — information disclosure of internal path structure that the previous host-only display intentionally omitted; the registrable-suffix logic is hand-rolled string splitting with no PSL awareness, so 'co.uk' style suffixes are also misjudged.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the profile display from a client-side host-only value (`website.split("/")[2]`) to a server-provided `website_name` (template now uses `model.website_name`). In `UserSerializer#website_name`, the “same-site” logic is hand-rolled via `split('.')` and includes the full `URI(...).path` not only when `website_host == discourse_host`, but also when the forum host ends with the website host (`discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)`) and when sibling subdomains share the same suffix after dropping the first label (the `split('.')[1..-1]` equality check). This can cause full path disclosure for unrelated tenants/departments under a shared parent domain and is not PSL-aware (e.g., `co.uk` cases), matching the finding’s concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The second branch of UserSerializer#website_name (equal label-count sibling subdomains, e.g. website_host 'www.example.com' vs discourse_host 'forum.example.com') has no test that triggers it. A regression in the sibling-subdomain comparison (app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:141-144) — e.g. the split/join logic returning the bare host or misjoining the path — passes the full suite because no spec exercises a same-label-count case; checked spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb in this diff, which only covers exact-host match, different-domain, and parent-domain cases, never the www-vs-forum branch the code explicitly implements and comments.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial branching logic in `UserSerializer#website_name` for the “same label-count sibling subdomains” case (`elsif (website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length) && discourse_host.split('.').length > 2`, with the `[1..-1].join('.')` comparison and potential `+ URI(...).path`). The added specs cover: different-domain (`discourse.org` vs `example.com`), exact-host match (`example.com`), and parent-domain (`forums.example.com` vs `example.com`). None sets both hosts to the same label count >2 (e.g., `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`) to exercise that explicit branch, so a regression there could indeed go untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The include_website_name guard (returns false when website is absent) is never tested, nor is the nil-return path when URI parsing fails. If website_name were emitted as a null key for users without a website (or the rescue-nil swallowed a case where website_name should be present), no spec fails; the existing 'with filled out website' context only asserts the present-website serialization, and there is no matching 'without website' context asserting json[:website_name] is absent.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial serializer logic `website_name` plus the conditional `include_website_name` (returns `website.present?`). The new specs only cover the "with filled out website" context and assert `json[:website_name]` values when `website` is present, but there is no spec asserting that `website_name` is omitted/absent when `website` is blank (i.e., exercising `include_website_name`). Additionally, `website_name` rescues URI parsing failures (`URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil`) and returns early on `website_host.nil?`, but no test covers an invalid/parse-failing website string to ensure behavior is correct. This is a specific missing-test gap introduced by the change, not a proven runtime bug.
